verifications.note: "The 0.3 Bcf/d Empire North Expansion Project, which increases deliverability to western New York consumers on the Empire Pipeline, entered partial service in late June [2020]." 0.3 Bcf/d = 300 MMcf/d, matching the recorded value exactly.
RBN Energy project entry: "Total Capacity: 300 MMcf/d" for the Empire North Expansion, in service Q3/2020.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirmed 300 MMcf/d as recorded, corroborated by an independent EIA analysis (govt.) and an independent RBN Energy project-tracker entry, both citing the Empire North Expansion specifically. Flag for the orchestrator: this 300 MMcf/d is the Empire North Expansion increment (25-mile, 26-inch reversal project, in service Q3/2020), not total system throughput — a 2002 National Fuel/SEC press release put the ORIGINAL 157-mile mainline's design capacity at 525 MMcf/d (see Start [ref] sources), a materially different number for the pre-expansion line. The sheet's recorded 300 MMcf/d matches the North Expansion figure exactly, so no correction proposed, but the discrepancy with the older 525 MMcf/d figure is worth the orchestrator's attention if 'Capacity' on this row is meant to represent total system capacity rather than the North Expansion increment.

verifications.note: "Empire owns and operates an approximately 269-mile bidirectional pipeline system" — matches recorded LengthKnown=269 exactly.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirmed 269 mi as recorded via National Fuel's own current operator page (the definitive source for the asset owner's total system length). Searched for a second, independent confirmation of the TOTAL 269-mile figure specifically: PHMSA's Alt-MAOP filing and the 2010 Federal Register notice (both in harvest_opened) only give individual-segment mileages (Empire Connector = 76.6 mi; Tuscarora Lateral notice = ~16 mi), not a system total; EIA's generic pipeline-data landing page does not carry a per-pipeline figure; this session's web-search budget was exhausted before a second total-length source could be located. The company's own segment history on the same page (157 + 77 + 15 + 17 = 266 mi across the original line, Empire Connector, Tioga County Extension, and Tuscarora Lateral, before accounting for the Empire North Expansion's compressor-only additions) is internally consistent with, and not materially different from, the ~269-mile total, but is not an independent second source since it's the same publisher. Single-source at medium tier per contract.

verifications.note: "Empire...originates at the United States/Canada border at the Chippawa Channel of the Niagara River" — confirms StartLocation=Chippawa, StartState/Province=Ontario, StartCountryOrArea=Canada.

"The 157-mile Empire line extends from the US-Canadian border at the Niagara River's Chippawa Channel to an interconnection point with other systems near Syracuse, NY" — independent trade-press confirmation of the Chippawa origin.

"...south from near Rochester, NY, into north-central Pennsylvania" and corporate-history text: "In November 2011, the 15-mile Tioga County Extension was constructed, extending the Empire Connector to producer-gathering systems located in Tioga County, PA" — confirms EndPrefecture/District=Tioga, EndState/Province=Pennsylvania, EndCountryOrArea=United States.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirmed as recorded: start at Chippawa, Ontario, Canada (the Chippawa Channel of the Niagara River, opposite Grand Island, NY, where the pipeline crosses into the US) per the 2002 SEC-filed press release and independent OGJ reporting; end in Tioga County, Pennsylvania, per National Fuel's own history of the Tioga County Extension (built 2011) that carried the system south into north-central PA. RBN Energy's Empire North Expansion entry (Capacity [ref] source) separately lists 'Destination: Chippawa, ON Canada' for that reversal sub-project, consistent with Chippawa being a physical terminus of the overall system (flow direction reversed for that project only).

verifications.note: "Empire Pipeline, Inc. (Empire)...is one of two FERC-regulated subsidiaries of National Fuel Gas Company...Empire owns and operates an approximately 269-mile...pipeline system" — Empire Pipeline, Inc. itself is stated to own and operate the asset.
"Empire Pipeline, Inc. (Empire) is operator of the Empire Connector Pipeline (ECP). National Fuel Gas Company is owner of Empire."

resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirmed Owner1=Empire Pipeline, 100% as recorded: National Fuel's own page states Empire Pipeline, Inc. owns and operates the system. Flag for the orchestrator (not treated as a contradiction): PHMSA's Alt-MAOP filing states the corporate-parent relationship the other way round -- 'National Fuel Gas Company is owner of Empire' -- i.e. National Fuel Gas Company (the NYSE-listed parent) wholly owns the special-purpose subsidiary Empire Pipeline, Inc., which in turn owns/operates the physical pipeline asset. Both statements are consistent (parent owns subsidiary; subsidiary owns pipeline) and the recorded Owner1 value (the subsidiary, 'Empire Pipeline') is the correct GEM convention for the asset-holding entity, but the ultimate parent (National Fuel Gas Company, NYSE: NFG) is worth having on file if the sheet ever wants a parent-company note.
